title: How to Skew Correct a Six-Sided Die
content:
## 1) Introduction
A method for skew-correcting a six-sided die can be found in the "A generalization to loaded dice" section within the article located at https://pit-claudel.fr/clement/blog/generating-uniformly-random-data-from-skewed-input-biased-coins-loaded-dice-skew-correction-and-the-von-neumann-extractor/

**This** particular article will use a worked example to *mathematically guarantee* 128 bits (for a 12 word seed phrease) or 256 bits (for a 24 word seed phrase) of entropy using a 6-sided die (d6).

In this article we will create a **12 word seed phrase**. Therefore we will need a total of **50** d6 values. These values are obtained by mapping sequences of triplet rolls according to their *order*

```
LMH=1, LHM=2, MHL=3, MLH=6, HLM=5, HML=4  
```
 
where L=Low, M=Middle, H=High. For example, the sequence 123 is in the order LMH. But so are all these other triplets

```
123, 124, 125, 126, 234, 235, 236, 345, 346, 456  
```

The premise behind this is that there are 3!=6 different ways to arrange the letters "L, M, H" and therefore can map all sequences to the numbers on a six-sided die.

The process is summarized below:

1) Roll a single six-sided die (d6) three times and record its values

2) Any triplet with distinct values is kept and mapped to the orderings described above (LMH, LHM, ...); any triplet with at least two of the same values is discarded

3) Repeat until we obtain 50 d6 values
## 2) A Small Example: 10 Trials

We will use 10 trials as a starting point. Let's say we rolled a d6 die three times and repeated this process 10 times to get the series of rolls

```
123 463 244 152 236 654 411 614 614 336
```

This gives us ten sequences of three digits. Any repeated digits within a sequence is discarded and the rest are mapped to one of the orderings.

```
LMH MHL X LHM LMH HML X HLM HLM X
```

Now the remaining are mapped to either 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6 according to the ordering maps above:

```
LMH=1 MHL=3 X LHM=2 LMH=1 HML=4 X HLM=5 HLM=5 X
```

Therefore out of 10 trials, we have obtained the 7 die rolls

```
1 3 2 1 4 5 5
```

*(Note we expect around 45% of these triplets to get discarded)*

## 3) A Big Example: 50 D6 Values

Let's assume we have continued this process until we have 50 rolls in total. Let's use this example:

```
136, 235, 425, 512, 124, 432, 523, 456, 456, 652, 532, 431, 651, 643, 314, 361, 145, 162, 145, 265, 365, 641, 143, 532, 531, 541, 146, 614, 461, 364, 126, 324, 256, 216, 214, 231, 126, 325, 524, 541, 265, 326, 436, 416, 634, 631, 461, 245, 356, 352
```

which has orderings

```
LMH, LMH, MLH, HLM, LMH, HML, HLM, LMH, LMH, HML, HML, HML, HML, HML, MLH, MHL, LMH, LHM, LMH, LHM, LHM, HML, LHM, HML, HML, HML, LMH, HLM, MHL, LHM, LMH, MLH, LMH, MLH, MLH, MHL, LMH, MLH, HLM, HML, LHM, MLH, MLH, MLH, HLM, HML, MHL, LMH, LMH, MHL
```

which maps to the die values

```
1, 1, 6, 5, 1, 4, 5, 1, 1, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4, 6, 3, 1, 2, 1, 2, 2, 4, 2, 4, 4, 4, 1, 5, 3, 2, 1, 6, 1, 6, 6, 3, 1, 6, 5, 4, 2, 6, 6, 6, 5, 4, 3, 1, 1, 3
```
## 4) How to Convert Your Rolls into a Seed Phrase 

### (a) The Short Way

Once you have your die rolls, put them all into a single string 
```
11651451144444631212242444153216166316542666543113
```
There are multiple options now to convert this string of d6 rolls into a seed phrase:

1) Enter it into a ColdCard   
**[Warning: you are trusting the ColdCard to give you the correct seed. Verify by using the tools listed in 3) and 4) below]**

2) Use a SeedSigner

3) Use Ian Coleman's BIP39 Tool (downloaded onto an airgapped computer). You can find this at https://iancoleman.io/bip39/

4) Use the Bitcoiner.Guide tool (again downloaded onto an airgapped computer). You can find this at https://bitcoiner.guide/seed/

If using Ian Coleman's tool, you click "Show entropy details", then paste the string (as shown above) into the box provided. Select "Base 10 [0-9]", then select "12 words" under the Mnemonic Length dropbox box. 

If using the Bitcoiner.Guide tool, go into "Seed Workspace" then click the Dice icon to "Enter your own entropy", then paste the string above into the box provided. Make sure **"12 words"** and **"Dice [1-6]"** are selected
### (b) The Long Way

Once you have your 50 rolls, we need to convert them into a 12 word seed phrase. In order to do this, we send the string of dice rolls through the SHA-256 hashing function. This gives us 256 bits and we keep the first 128 of them for our 12 word seed.

In any linux machine, we can type

```
echo -n "11651451144444631212242444153216166316542666543113" | sha256sum  
```
to get the output (in hex)
```
375b26bdb3e85c176decb8e3988606254f9b9cabf8dbab080d3badf394faf90f
```
This is a string of 64 hex digits, which equates to 256 bits. However, we only need 128 bits, which is the first 32 hex digits:
```
375b26bdb3e85c176decb8e398860625
```
To convert this to binary (using CAPITAL letters)
```
echo "obase=2; ibase=16; 375B26BDB3E85C176DECB8E398860625" | bc
```
and get
```
110111010110110010011010111101101100111110100001011100000101110110110111101100101110001110001110011000100001100000011000100101
```
Note: since 3 in hex (the first digit of our string) is 0011 in binary, you are actually missing the leading zeros and thus the above string is only 126 bits. So we add 00 to the beginning of the binary string to get
```
00110111010110110010011010111101101100111110100001011100000101110110110111101100101110001110001110011000100001100000011000100101
```
and now have a 128-bit string.


From this point, follow MrRGnome's guide on converting a 128 bit string to seed words at https://btcmaxis.com/article.html?id=ca2d1009-d3be-49b2-9879-8aa69f8fde77

You should obtain the seed phrase  
```
dance summer quarter guitar magic arm response novel toe service light enough
```
